v: The oracle[^1] that Habakkuk the prophet saw.[^2]
הַמַּשָׂא֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה חֲבַקּ֖וּק הַנָּבִֽיא׃
How long, Yahweh,[^3] must I cry for help, and you do not listen? I cry out to you, "Violence!" but you do not save.
עַד־אָ֧נָה יְהוָ֛ה שִׁוַּ֖עְתִּי וְלֹ֣א תִשְׁמָ֑ע אֶזְעַ֥ק אֵלֶ֛יךָ חָמָ֖ס וְלֹ֥א תוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃
Why do you make me see wickedness, and why do you look on trouble?[^4] Destruction and violence are before me; there is strife, and conflict rises up.
לָ֣מָּה תַרְאֵ֤נִי אָ֙וֶן֙ וְעָמָ֣ל תַּבִּ֔יט וְשֹׁ֥ד וְחָמָ֖ס לְנֶגְדִּ֑י וַיְהִ֧י רִ֦יב וּמָד֖וֹן יִשָּֽׂא׃
So the law[^5] grows numb, and justice never goes out. For the wicked surround the righteous, so justice goes out twisted.
עַל־כֵּן֙ תָּפ֣וּג תּוֹרָ֔ה וְלֹֽא־יֵצֵ֥א לָנֶ֖צַח מִשְׁפָּ֑ט כִּ֤י רָשָׁע֙ מַכְתִּ֣יר אֶת־הַצַּדִּ֔יק עַל־כֵּ֛ן יֵצֵ֥א מִשְׁפָּ֖ט מְעֻקָּֽל׃
"Look among the nations and see![^6] Be astonished, be amazed! For I am doing a deed[^7] in your days that you would not believe if you were told.
רְא֤וּ בַגּוֹיִם֙ וְֽהַבִּ֔יטוּ וְהִֽתַּמְּה֖וּ תְּמָ֑הוּ כִּי־פֹ֙עַל֙ פֹּעֵ֣ל בִּֽימֵיכֶ֔ם לֹ֥א תַאֲמִ֖ינוּ כִּ֥י יְסֻפָּֽר׃
For look, I am raising up the Babylonians,[^8] that bitter and hasty nation, which marches through the breadth of the earth to seize dwellings that are not its own.
כִּֽי־הִנְנִ֤י מֵקִים֙ אֶת־הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים הַגּ֖וֹי הַמַּ֣ר וְהַנִּמְהָ֑ר הַֽהוֹלֵךְ֙ לְמֶרְחֲבֵי־אֶ֔רֶץ לָרֶ֖שֶׁת מִשְׁכָּנ֥וֹת לֹּא־לֽוֹ׃
They are dreaded and feared; their justice and their dignity come from themselves.[^9]
אָיֹ֥ם וְנוֹרָ֖א ה֑וּא מִמֶּ֕נּוּ מִשְׁפָּט֥וֹ וּשְׂאֵת֖וֹ יֵצֵֽא׃
Their horses are swifter than leopards and fiercer than wolves at evening.[^10] Their horsemen gallop on;[^11] their horsemen come from far away. They fly like an eagle swooping to devour.
וְקַלּ֨וּ מִנְּמֵרִ֜ים סוּסָ֗יו וְחַדּוּ֙ מִזְּאֵ֣בֵי עֶ֔רֶב וּפָ֖שׁוּ פָּֽרָשָׁ֑יו וּפָֽרָשָׁיו֙ מֵרָח֣וֹק יָבֹ֔אוּ יָעֻ֕פוּ כְּנֶ֖שֶׁר חָ֥שׁ לֶאֱכֽוֹל׃
They all come for violence; their faces press forward like the east wind,[^12] and they gather captives like sand.
כֻּלֹּה֙ לְחָמָ֣ס יָב֔וֹא מְגַמַּ֥ת פְּנֵיהֶ֖ם קָדִ֑ימָה וַיֶּאֱסֹ֥ף כַּח֖וֹל שֶֽׁבִי׃
They scoff at kings, and rulers are a joke to them. They laugh at every fortress; they heap up earth[^13] and capture it.
וְהוּא֙ בַּמְּלָכִ֣ים יִתְקַלָּ֔ס וְרֹזְנִ֖ים מִשְׂחָ֣ק ל֑וֹ ה֚וּא לְכָל־מִבְצָ֣ר יִשְׂחָ֔ק וַיִּצְבֹּ֥ר עָפָ֖ר וַֽיִּלְכְּדָֽהּ׃
Then they sweep past like the wind and go on, guilty men, whose own strength is their god."[^14]
אָ֣ז חָלַ֥ף ר֛וּחַ וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֖ר וְאָשֵׁ֑ם ז֥וּ כֹח֖וֹ לֵאלֹהֽוֹ׃
Are you not from of old, Yahweh, my God, my Holy One? We will not die.[^15] Yahweh, you have appointed them to execute judgment; Rock,[^16] you have established them to punish.
הֲל֧וֹא אַתָּ֣ה מִקֶּ֗דֶם יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהַ֛י קְדֹשִׁ֖י לֹ֣א נָמ֑וּת יְהוָה֙ לְמִשְׁפָּ֣ט שַׂמְתּ֔וֹ וְצ֖וּר לְהוֹכִ֥יחַ יְסַדְתּֽוֹ׃
Your eyes are too pure to look on evil, and you cannot look on wrongdoing. Why then do you look on the treacherous and keep silent when the wicked swallow up those more righteous than they?
טְה֤וֹר עֵינַ֙יִם֙ מֵרְא֣וֹת רָ֔ע וְהַבִּ֥יט אֶל־עָמָ֖ל לֹ֣א תוּכָ֑ל לָ֤מָּה תַבִּיט֙ בּֽוֹגְדִ֔ים תַּחֲרִ֕ישׁ בְּבַלַּ֥ע רָשָׁ֖ע צַדִּ֥יק מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
You have made human beings like the fish of the sea, like creeping things that have no ruler.
וַתַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אָדָ֖ם כִּדְגֵ֣י הַיָּ֑ם כְּרֶ֖מֶשׂ לֹא־מֹשֵׁ֥ל בּֽוֹ׃
He[^17] brings all of them up with a hook; he drags them out with his net and gathers them in his dragnet. So he rejoices and is glad.
כֻּלֹּה֙ בְּחַכָּ֣ה הֵֽעֲלָ֔ה יְגֹרֵ֣הוּ בְחֶרְמ֔וֹ וְיַאַסְפֵ֖הוּ בְּמִכְמַרְתּ֑וֹ עַל־כֵּ֖ן יִשְׂמַ֥ח וְיָגִֽיל׃
That is why he sacrifices to his net and burns incense to his dragnet, for by them his portion is rich and his food is plentiful.[^18]
עַל־כֵּן֙ יְזַבֵּ֣חַ לְחֶרְמ֔וֹ וִֽיקַטֵּ֖ר לְמִכְמַרְתּ֑וֹ כִּ֤י בָהֵ֙מָּה֙ שָׁמֵ֣ן חֶלְק֔וֹ וּמַאֲכָל֖וֹ בְּרִאָֽה׃
Will he therefore keep emptying his net[^19] and go on killing nations without mercy?
הַ֥עַל כֵּ֖ן יָרִ֣יק חֶרְמ֑וֹ וְתָמִ֛יד לַהֲרֹ֥ג גּוֹיִ֖ם לֹ֥א יַחְמֽוֹל׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *massa*, from the verb "to lift up, carry": a message "lifted up" by the prophet, or a "burden" laid on a nation. Traditionally "the burden".
n.2: Nothing certain is known of Habakkuk. He probably prophesied in the last years of the seventh century BC, when the Babylonians were rising to power (verse 6). The book is a dialogue: Habakkuk complains (1:2–4), Yahweh answers (1:5–11), Habakkuk complains again (1:12–17), and Yahweh answers again (2:2–20). Because the speakers alternate, Yahweh's replies are put in quotation marks.
n.3: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.4: Or "Why do you make me look on trouble?"
n.6: The Septuagint reads "Look, you scoffers", and Paul quotes this verse in that form in Acts 13:41.
n.7: Literally "a deed is doing". *I* is supplied from verse 6.
n.8: Hebrew *Kasdim*, traditionally "Chaldeans": the people of southern Mesopotamia whose kings then ruled Babylon. Their new empire began in 626 BC, and under Nebuchadnezzar they defeated Egypt at Carchemish in 605 BC.
n.9: That is, they recognize no law but their own.
n.10: Wolves that hunt at nightfall, hungry after the day (Zephaniah 3:3).
n.11: The meaning of the Hebrew verb is uncertain. Perhaps "paw the ground" or "spring forward".
n.12: The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain. Literally "the eagerness of their faces is eastward" or "forward".
n.13: A siege ramp, built up against the city wall.
n.14: The Hebrew is difficult. Literally "Then a wind passes on and goes through, and is guilty, this one whose strength is his god".
n.15: This is one of the *tiqqune sopherim*, the rabbinic "corrections of the scribes": the tradition says that the text once read "You will not die" and was changed out of reverence for God.
n.16: A title of God, the one on whom his people can rely (Deuteronomy 32:4).
n.17: The Babylonian conqueror, pictured as a fisherman.
n.18: Literally "his portion is fat and his food is fat".
n.19: The Habakkuk commentary found at Qumran (1QpHab) reads "his sword".

v: I will stand at my watch post and station myself on the rampart. I will watch to see what he will say to me,[^1] and what I will answer concerning my complaint.[^2]
עַל־מִשְׁמַרְתִּ֣י אֶעֱמֹ֔דָה וְאֶֽתְיַצְּבָ֖ה עַל־מָצ֑וֹר וַאֲצַפֶּ֗ה לִרְאוֹת֙ מַה־יְדַבֶּר־בִּ֔י וּמָ֥ה אָשִׁ֖יב עַל־תּוֹכַחְתִּֽי׃
Then Yahweh[^3] answered me: "Write down the vision; make it plain on tablets, so that the one who reads it may run.[^4]
וַיַּעֲנֵ֤נִי יְהוָה֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר כְּת֣וֹב חָז֔וֹן וּבָאֵ֖ר עַל־הַלֻּח֑וֹת לְמַ֥עַן יָר֖וּץ ק֥וֹרֵא בֽוֹ׃
For the vision is still for the appointed time. It hurries[^5] toward the end, and it will not lie. If it seems slow, wait for it; it will surely come, it will not delay.
כִּ֣י ע֤וֹד חָזוֹן֙ לַמּוֹעֵ֔ד וְיָפֵ֥חַ לַקֵּ֖ץ וְלֹ֣א יְכַזֵּ֑ב אִם־יִתְמַהְמָהּ֙ חַכֵּה־ל֔וֹ כִּֽי־בֹ֥א יָבֹ֖א לֹ֥א יְאַחֵֽר׃
Look, his soul is puffed up;[^6] it is not upright within him. But the righteous will live by his faithfulness.[^7]
הִנֵּ֣ה עֻפְּלָ֔ה לֹא־יָשְׁרָ֥ה נַפְשׁ֖וֹ בּ֑וֹ וְצַדִּ֖יק בֶּאֱמוּנָת֥וֹ יִחְיֶֽה׃

Moreover, wine[^8] is treacherous; the arrogant man will not rest.[^9] He opens his throat as wide as Sheol;[^10] like death, he is never satisfied. He gathers all the nations for himself and collects all the peoples for himself.

וְאַף֙ כִּֽי־הַיַּ֣יִן בּוֹגֵ֔ד גֶּ֥בֶר יָהִ֖יר וְלֹ֣א יִנְוֶ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֩ הִרְחִ֨יב כִּשְׁא֜וֹל נַפְשׁ֗וֹ וְה֤וּא כַמָּ֙וֶת֙ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׂבָּ֔ע וַיֶּאֱסֹ֤ף אֵלָיו֙ כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וַיִּקְבֹּ֥ץ אֵלָ֖יו כָּל־הָעַמִּֽים׃

Will not all of them take up a taunt[^11] against him, with mocking riddles about him, and say: 'Woe to[^12] him who heaps up what is not his own (how long?) and loads himself with goods taken in pledge![^13]
הֲלוֹא־אֵ֣לֶּה כֻלָּ֗ם עָלָיו֙ מָשָׁ֣ל יִשָּׂ֔אוּ וּמְלִיצָ֖ה חִיד֣וֹת ל֑וֹ וְיֹאמַ֗ר ה֚וֹי הַמַּרְבֶּ֣ה לֹּא־ל֔וֹ עַד־מָתַ֕י וּמַכְבִּ֥יד עָלָ֖יו עַבְטִֽיט׃
Will not your creditors[^14] suddenly rise up, and those who make you tremble wake up? Then you will become plunder for them.
הֲל֣וֹא פֶ֗תַע יָק֙וּמוּ֙ נֹשְׁכֶ֔יךָ וְיִקְצ֖וּ מְזַעְזְעֶ֑יךָ וְהָיִ֥יתָ לִמְשִׁסּ֖וֹת לָֽמוֹ׃
Because you have plundered many nations, all the rest of the peoples will plunder you, because of the blood of human beings and violence done to the earth, to the city and all who live in it.[^15]
כִּֽי אַתָּ֤ה שַׁלּ֙וֹתָ֙ גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֔ים יְשָׁלּ֖וּךָ כָּל־יֶ֣תֶר עַמִּ֑ים מִדְּמֵ֤י אָדָם֙ וַחֲמַס־אֶ֔רֶץ קִרְיָ֖ה וְכָל־יֹ֥שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ׃ פ
Woe to him who gets evil gain for his house, to set his nest on high and escape from the grasp of disaster!
ה֗וֹי בֹּצֵ֛עַ בֶּ֥צַע רָ֖ע לְבֵית֑וֹ לָשׂ֤וּם בַּמָּרוֹם֙ קִנּ֔וֹ לְהִנָּצֵ֖ל מִכַּף־רָֽע׃
You have planned shame for your house by cutting off many peoples; you have sinned against your own life.[^16]
יָעַ֥צְתָּ בֹּ֖שֶׁת לְבֵיתֶ֑ךָ קְצוֹת־עַמִּ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים וְחוֹטֵ֥א נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃
For the stone will cry out from the wall, and the beam[^17] will answer it from the woodwork.
כִּי־אֶ֖בֶן מִקִּ֣יר תִּזְעָ֑ק וְכָפִ֖יס מֵעֵ֥ץ יַעֲנֶֽנָּה׃ פ
Woe to him who builds a city with bloodshed and founds a town on injustice![^18]
ה֛וֹי בֹּנֶ֥ה עִ֖יר בְּדָמִ֑ים וְכוֹנֵ֥ן קִרְיָ֖ה בְּעַוְלָֽה׃
Is it not from Yahweh of Armies[^19] that peoples wear themselves out only for the fire, and nations exhaust themselves for nothing?[^20]
הֲל֣וֹא הִנֵּ֔ה מֵאֵ֖ת יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וְיִֽיגְע֤וּ עַמִּים֙ בְּדֵי־אֵ֔שׁ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים בְּדֵי־רִ֥יק יִעָֽפוּ׃
For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of Yahweh, as the waters cover the sea.[^21]
כִּ֚י תִּמָּלֵ֣א הָאָ֔רֶץ לָדַ֖עַת אֶת־כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֑ה כַּמַּ֖יִם יְכַסּ֥וּ עַל־יָֽם׃ ס
Woe to him who makes his neighbors drink, pouring out your wrath[^22] and making them drunk, in order to gaze on their nakedness![^23]
ה֚וֹי מַשְׁקֵ֣ה רֵעֵ֔הוּ מְסַפֵּ֥חַ חֲמָתְךָ֖ וְאַ֣ף שַׁכֵּ֑ר לְמַ֥עַן הַבִּ֖יט עַל־מְעוֹרֵיהֶֽם׃
You will be filled with shame instead of glory. Drink, you too, and show your foreskin![^24] The cup in Yahweh's right hand will come around to you, and utter disgrace[^25] will cover your glory.
שָׂבַ֤עְתָּ קָלוֹן֙ מִכָּב֔וֹד שְׁתֵ֥ה גַם־אַ֖תָּה וְהֵֽעָרֵ֑ל תִּסּ֣וֹב עָלֶ֗יךָ כּ֚וֹס יְמִ֣ין יְהוָ֔ה וְקִיקָל֖וֹן עַל־כְּבוֹדֶֽךָ׃

For the violence done to Lebanon[^26] will overwhelm you, and the destruction of the animals will terrify you,[^27] because of the blood of human beings and violence done to the earth, to the city and all who live in it.
כִּ֣י חֲמַ֤ס לְבָנוֹן֙ יְכַסֶּ֔ךָּ וְשֹׁ֥ד בְּהֵמ֖וֹת יְחִיתַ֑ן מִדְּמֵ֤י אָדָם֙ וַחֲמַס־אֶ֔רֶץ קִרְיָ֖ה וְכָל־יֹ֥שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ׃ ס
What use is a carved image, once its maker has carved it, or a cast image, a teacher of lies? For its maker trusts in what he has made himself, when he makes idols that cannot speak.[^28]
מָֽה־הוֹעִ֣יל פֶּ֗סֶל כִּ֤י פְסָלוֹ֙ יֹֽצְר֔וֹ מַסֵּכָ֖ה וּמ֣וֹרֶה שָּׁ֑קֶר כִּ֣י בָטַ֞ח יֹצֵ֤ר יִצְרוֹ֙ עָלָ֔יו לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת אֱלִילִ֥ים אִלְּמִֽים׃ ס
Woe to him who says to a piece of wood, "Wake up!" and to a silent stone, "Get up!" Can it teach? Look, it is overlaid with gold and silver, but there is no breath[^29] in it at all.'
ה֣וֹי אֹמֵ֤ר לָעֵץ֙ הָקִ֔יצָה ע֖וּרִי לְאֶ֣בֶן דּוּמָ֑ם ה֣וּא יוֹרֶ֔ה הִנֵּה־ה֗וּא תָּפוּשׂ֙ זָהָ֣ב וָכֶ֔סֶף וְכָל־ר֖וּחַ אֵ֥ין בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃
But Yahweh is in his holy temple. Let all the earth be silent before him."[^30]
וַֽיהוָ֖ה בְּהֵיכַ֣ל קָדְשׁ֑וֹ הַ֥ס מִפָּנָ֖יו כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃ פ

n.1: Literally "what he will speak in me".
n.3: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.4: Perhaps "so that a herald may run with it", carrying the message, or "so that it can be read easily".
n.5: Literally "it pants". Or "it testifies": the Hebrew word can also mean "witness".
n.6: The meaning of the Hebrew word, *uppelah*, is uncertain. The Septuagint reads "If he shrinks back, my soul takes no pleasure in him".
n.7: Hebrew *emunah*, "faithfulness, steadiness, firmness", from the same root as *amen*. It describes a person who holds firm and can be relied on, and here may mean steady trust in God while waiting for the vision. Or "by his faith". *His* may also refer to God or to the vision. The Septuagint reads "the righteous will live by my faithfulness", that is, God's. Paul quotes the line as "The righteous will live by faith" (Romans 1:17; Galatians 3:11), and Hebrews 10:37–38 quotes verses 3–4 from the Septuagint, with the lines of verse 4 in the reverse order: "my righteous one will live by faith, and if he shrinks back, my soul takes no pleasure in him". Greek *pistis* means both "faith" and "faithfulness".
n.8: The Habakkuk commentary found at Qumran (1QpHab) reads "wealth".
n.9: The meaning of the Hebrew verb is uncertain. Perhaps "will not reach his goal" or "will not stay at home".
n.10: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead. *Throat* is Hebrew *nephesh*, here the appetite.
n.11: Hebrew *mashal*, a saying or proverb, here a mocking song. It runs through verse 19, as five cries of "Woe to" (verses 6, 9, 12, 15 and 19).
n.12: Hebrew *hoy*, a cry of mourning for the dead ("Alas!", 1 Kings 13:30). The prophets use it to announce disaster, and in that sense it is translated "Woe to".
n.13: Hebrew *avtit*, found only here, from *avot*, "pledge": goods taken as security for loans. It sounds like *av tit*, "thick mud".
n.14: Literally "those who bite you". The Hebrew word for interest on a loan, *neshekh*, also means "bite".
n.15: Literally "to the earth, a city and all who live in it". Also in verse 17.
n.17: Hebrew *kafis*, found only here, probably a rafter or beam. Compare Luke 19:40.
n.19: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.20: Nearly the same words are found in Jeremiah 51:58.
n.22: Hebrew *chemah*, "wrath" or "poison". Some scholars read "from your wineskin", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.23: The Habakkuk commentary found at Qumran (1QpHab) reads "their festivals".
n.24: Hebrew *he'arel*, "show yourself uncircumcised". The Habakkuk commentary found at Qumran (1QpHab), the Septuagint and the Syriac read "and stagger", a word with two of the same letters in the reverse order.
n.25: Hebrew *qiqalon*, found only here, a stronger form of *qalon*, "shame", in the first line.
n.26: The cedar forests of Lebanon were cut down by conquerors for their building projects (Isaiah 14:8; 37:24).
n.27: Literally "will terrify them". The Hebrew form is unusual.
n.28: A play on words: *elilim illemim*, "mute idols". *A teacher of lies* may refer to oracles sought from idols.
n.30: Literally "Hush before him, all the earth!" Compare Zephaniah 1:7; Zechariah 2:17 (2:13 in most English Bibles).

v: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet. According to Shigionoth.[^1]
תְּפִלָּ֖ה לַחֲבַקּ֣וּק הַנָּבִ֑יא עַ֖ל שִׁגְיֹנֽוֹת׃
Yahweh,[^2] I have heard the report of you; I stand in awe, Yahweh, of your work.[^3] In the midst of the years revive it; in the midst of the years make it known.[^4] In wrath, remember mercy.
יְהוָ֗ה שָׁמַ֣עְתִּי שִׁמְעֲךָ֮ יָרֵאתִי֒ יְהוָ֗ה פָּֽעָלְךָ֙ בְּקֶ֤רֶב שָׁנִים֙ חַיֵּ֔יהוּ בְּקֶ֥רֶב שָׁנִ֖ים תּוֹדִ֑יעַ בְּרֹ֖גֶז רַחֵ֥ם תִּזְכּֽוֹר׃
God[^5] came from Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran.[^6] Selah.[^7] His splendor covered the heavens, and the earth was full of his praise.[^8]
אֱל֙וֹהַ֙ מִתֵּימָ֣ן יָב֔וֹא וְקָד֥וֹשׁ מֵֽהַר־פָּארָ֖ן סֶ֑לָה כִּסָּ֤ה שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ הוֹד֔וֹ וּתְהִלָּת֖וֹ מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָֽרֶץ׃
His brightness was like the light; rays came from his hand,[^9] and there his power was hidden.
וְנֹ֙גַהּ֙ כָּא֣וֹר תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה קַרְנַ֥יִם מִיָּד֖וֹ ל֑וֹ וְשָׁ֖ם חֶבְי֥וֹן עֻזֹּֽה׃
Plague went before him, and pestilence[^10] followed at his heels.
לְפָנָ֖יו יֵ֣לֶךְ דָּ֑בֶר וְיֵצֵ֥א רֶ֖שֶׁף לְרַגְלָֽיו׃
He stood and measured[^11] the earth; he looked and made the nations tremble. The ancient mountains were shattered; the everlasting hills sank down. His ways are as of old.[^12]
עָמַ֣ד ׀ וַיְמֹ֣דֶד אֶ֗רֶץ רָאָה֙ וַיַּתֵּ֣ר גּוֹיִ֔ם וַיִּתְפֹּֽצְצוּ֙ הַרְרֵי־עַ֔ד שַׁח֖וּ גִּבְע֣וֹת עוֹלָ֑ם הֲלִיכ֥וֹת עוֹלָ֖ם לֽוֹ׃
I saw the tents of Cushan in distress;[^13] the tent curtains of the land of Midian trembled.
תַּ֣חַת אָ֔וֶן רָאִ֖יתִי אָהֳלֵ֣י כוּשָׁ֑ן יִרְגְּז֕וּן יְרִיע֖וֹת אֶ֥רֶץ מִדְיָֽן׃ ס
Was your anger against the rivers, Yahweh? Was your wrath against the rivers, or your fury against the sea,[^14] when you rode on your horses, on your chariots of victory?
הֲבִנְהָרִים֙ חָרָ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה אִ֤ם בַּנְּהָרִים֙ אַפֶּ֔ךָ אִם־בַּיָּ֖ם עֶבְרָתֶ֑ךָ כִּ֤י תִרְכַּב֙ עַל־סוּסֶ֔יךָ מַרְכְּבֹתֶ֖יךָ יְשׁוּעָֽה׃
Your bow was laid bare; arrows were sworn by your word.[^15] Selah. You split the earth with rivers.
עֶרְיָ֤ה תֵעוֹר֙ קַשְׁתֶּ֔ךָ שְׁבֻע֥וֹת מַטּ֖וֹת אֹ֣מֶר סֶ֑לָה נְהָר֖וֹת תְּבַקַּע־אָֽרֶץ׃
The mountains saw you and writhed; a torrent of water swept by.[^16] The deep gave its voice; it lifted its hands on high.
רָא֤וּךָ יָחִ֙ילוּ֙ הָרִ֔ים זֶ֥רֶם מַ֖יִם עָבָ֑ר נָתַ֤ן תְּהוֹם֙ קוֹל֔וֹ ר֖וֹם יָדֵ֥יהוּ נָשָֽׂא׃
Sun and moon stood still in their dwelling[^17] at the light of your arrows as they flew, at the flash of your glittering spear.
שֶׁ֥מֶשׁ יָרֵ֖חַ עָ֣מַד זְבֻ֑לָה לְא֤וֹר חִצֶּ֙יךָ֙ יְהַלֵּ֔כוּ לְנֹ֖גַהּ בְּרַ֥ק חֲנִיתֶֽךָ׃
In fury you marched through the earth; in anger you trampled the nations.
בְּזַ֖עַם תִּצְעַד־אָ֑רֶץ בְּאַ֖ף תָּד֥וּשׁ גּוֹיִֽם׃
You went out to save your people, to save your anointed one.[^18] You crushed the head of the house of the wicked, laying it bare from foundation to neck.[^19] Selah.
יָצָ֙אתָ֙ לְיֵ֣שַׁע עַמֶּ֔ךָ לְיֵ֖שַׁע אֶת־מְשִׁיחֶ֑ךָ מָחַ֤צְתָּ רֹּאשׁ֙ מִבֵּ֣ית רָשָׁ֔ע עָר֛וֹת יְס֥וֹד עַד־צַוָּ֖אר סֶֽלָה׃ פ
With his own arrows you pierced the head of his warriors,[^20] who stormed out to scatter me, gloating as if about to devour the poor in secret.
נָקַ֤בְתָּ בְמַטָּיו֙ רֹ֣אשׁ *פרזו **פְּרָזָ֔יו יִסְעֲר֖וּ לַהֲפִיצֵ֑נִי עֲלִ֣יצֻתָ֔ם כְּמוֹ־לֶאֱכֹ֥ל עָנִ֖י בַּמִּסְתָּֽר׃
You trampled the sea with your horses, churning the mighty waters.
דָּרַ֥כְתָּ בַיָּ֖ם סוּסֶ֑יךָ חֹ֖מֶר מַ֥יִם רַבִּֽים׃

I heard, and my body trembled;[^21] my lips quivered at the sound. Rottenness entered my bones, and my legs trembled beneath me. Yet I will wait quietly[^22] for the day of distress to come on the people who invade us.
שָׁמַ֣עְתִּי ׀ וַתִּרְגַּ֣ז בִּטְנִ֗י לְקוֹל֙ צָלֲל֣וּ שְׂפָתַ֔י יָב֥וֹא רָקָ֛ב בַּעֲצָמַ֖י וְתַחְתַּ֣י אֶרְגָּ֑ז אֲשֶׁ֤ר אָנ֙וּחַ֙ לְי֣וֹם צָרָ֔ה לַעֲל֖וֹת לְעַ֥ם יְגוּדֶֽנּוּ׃

Though the fig tree does not blossom, and there is no fruit on the vines, though the olive crop fails, and the fields produce no food, though the flock is cut off from the fold, and there are no cattle in the stalls,
כִּֽי־תְאֵנָ֣ה לֹֽא־תִפְרָ֗ח וְאֵ֤ין יְבוּל֙ בַּגְּפָנִ֔ים כִּחֵשׁ֙ מַעֲשֵׂה־זַ֔יִת וּשְׁדֵמ֖וֹת לֹא־עָ֣שָׂה אֹ֑כֶל גָּזַ֤ר מִמִּכְלָה֙ צֹ֔אן וְאֵ֥ין בָּקָ֖ר בָּרְפָתִֽים׃
yet I will rejoice in Yahweh; I will be joyful in the God of my salvation.
וַאֲנִ֖י בַּיהוָ֣ה אֶעְל֑וֹזָה אָגִ֖ילָה בֵּאלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׁעִֽי׃
Yahweh, the Lord,[^23] is my strength. He makes my feet like the feet of a deer, and makes me walk on my heights.[^24] For the director. With my stringed instruments.[^25]
יְהוִ֤הּ אֲדֹנָי֙ חֵילִ֔י וַיָּ֤שֶׂם רַגְלַי֙ כָּֽאַיָּל֔וֹת וְעַ֥ל בָּמוֹתַ֖י יַדְרִכֵ֑נִי לַמְנַצֵּ֖חַ בִּנְגִינוֹתָֽי׃

n.1: Hebrew *shigyonot*, the plural of *shiggayon* (Psalm 7:1), a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps a lament, or a song with a changing rhythm. This chapter is a psalm, with a title, the word *Selah* (verses 3, 9 and 13) and a note for the musicians at the end (verse 19), like the psalms of the book of Psalms.
n.2: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.3: Or "Yahweh, I have heard of your fame; I fear, Yahweh, your work."
n.4: The Septuagint reads "In the midst of two living creatures you will be known", reading the Hebrew words for "years" and "revive it" differently.
n.5: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic word for God.
n.6: Teman, in Edom, and Mount Paran, in the wilderness south of Judah, lay on the way from Sinai. Yahweh is pictured coming from the south, as in Deuteronomy 33:2 and Judges 5:4–5. The verbs in verses 3–15 may describe what Yahweh did in the past, at the exodus and at Sinai, or what he will do.
n.7: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verses 9 and 13.
n.9: Literally "horns from his hand were his". The same word is used of the rays of light from Moses' face (Exodus 34:29–30).
n.10: Hebrew *deber* and *resheph*. Resheph was the name of a Canaanite god of plague. Here plague and pestilence attend Yahweh like servants.
n.11: Or "shook". The same consonants can be read either way.
n.12: Or "Ancient paths are his", or "His ways are everlasting".
n.13: Literally "under trouble". Cushan was probably a people living near Midian, in the desert east and south of Edom.
n.14: The waters that Yahweh divided at the Red Sea and at the Jordan (Psalm 114:3–5), and the sea as the power of chaos that he overcomes (Psalm 74:13–14).
n.15: The Hebrew is very difficult. Literally "oaths of rods, a word". *Rods* may mean "arrows" (verse 14) or "tribes".
n.16: Compare Psalm 77:17–19 (77:16–18 in most English Bibles).
n.18: Hebrew *mashiach*, a king or priest anointed with oil, here probably the king of Israel, or the people as a whole.
n.19: Literally "laying bare the foundation up to the neck". The picture moves between a house and a body.
n.20: Literally "With his rods you pierced the head of his warriors". The Hebrew text is written "his warrior" but read "his warriors". The meaning of the word for warriors, *perazav*, is uncertain.
n.22: Or "I must wait quietly". Hebrew *anuach*, "I will rest".
n.24: Nearly the same words are found in Psalm 18:34 (18:33 in most English Bibles).
n.25: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music, a note found at the head of many psalms (Psalm 4:1). Here it closes the psalm.
